query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the Pd/Pt component in FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with Cr will increase the coercivity by promoting higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy and enhanced domain wall pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) alloy exhibiting a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure with soft ferromagnetism (low coercivity) and high saturation magnetization.
generation.intervention: Substitute the soft-magnetic Pd/Pt element with Cr to form an almost equiatomic (Fe, Co, Ni, Cr) high-entropy alloy while maintaining a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
generation.conditions: The alloy should be synthesized via arc melting with rapid solidification and controlled annealing to secure a homogeneous equiatomic distribution and high configurational entropy. Processing parameters must avoid phase separation and maintain a single-phase structure.
generation.structural_mediator: The introduction of Cr is expected to favor the formation of a chemically modulated or slightly lower-symmetry structure compared to the pristine fcc phase. Such microstructural modifications can generate local strain fields and heterogeneity that serve as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
generation.mechanism: Cr possesses higher intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy compared to Pd/Pt. When introduced into the alloy, Cr can increase the local anisotropy energy and promote stronger domain wall pinning. This intervention is predicted to counter the innate soft-magnetic behavior by increasing the energy barrier for domain wall motion, thereby raising the coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiCr alloy will show an increase in coercivity relative to the FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) baseline while retaining high saturation magnetization. Although the exact magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain, a statistically significant enhancement (e.g., at least a 50% increase) is expected under optimized synthesis conditions.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) high-entropy alloy produced via arc melting and controlled annealing that exhibits low coercivity (soft ferromagnetism) and high saturation magnetization.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to equiatomic, high-entropy alloys synthesized under conditions that ensure a single-phase structure and high configurational entropy (≥1.0R). Deviations in composition or processing that lead to phase separation or significant changes in microstructure may not exhibit the predicted magnetic behavior.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative increase in coercivity is uncertain, and there may be trade-offs with slight reductions in saturation magnetization. The influence of possible changes in microstructural ordering on the overall magnetic properties also remains to be fully determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloys: one set with the baseline equiatomic FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) alloy and another set with Cr substituted for Pd/Pt to form an equiatomic FeCoNiCr alloy. Both sets should be synthesized using identical arc melting, rapid solidification, and controlled annealing protocols to ensure high configurational entropy and single-phase formation. Characterize their microstructure using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron microscopy to confirm phase purity and homogeneity. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops using SQUID or vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM) to extract coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCoNiCr alloy is not statistically significantly higher (e.g., less than a 50% increase) than that of the FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, if unexpected phase separations or deterioration in magnetic order are observed, the proposed mechanism would be challenged.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.
